question: In response to the adverse effects caused by the Russian aggression towards Ukraine, in July 2022, an amendment to the European Maritime and Fisheries Fund (EMFF) Regulation was adopted so that additional funding could be provided for the primary, processing and marketing sectors in the fisheries and aquaculture industries. In the light of the above: 1.
Will the Commission extend the period provided for businesses to cover expenditure incurred in 2023?
To enable the competent authorities to offer compensation again for the additional costs incurred in 2023, will Member States be able to have an extraordinary item in 2024?
answer: The European Maritime and Fisheries Fund Regulation (EMFF) was amended on 27 July 2022. This amendment allows Member States to provide support under the EMFF for businesses to cover increased operating costs, in case of expenditure incurred between 24 February 2022 (date of the initial Russian invasion of Ukraine) and 31 December 2023, which is the end of the eligibility period for all financing under the EMFF.

Additional support is available under the crisis mechanism of the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF) for expenditure incurred between 24 February 2022 and 31 December 2022. Further support can be provided to operators by the Member States under the Temporary Crisis and Transition Framework for State Aid (1).

Certain sections of this framework remain in force until the end of 2025, with specific support related to the additional costs due to the high gas and electricity prices available until 30 June 2024.

Communication from the Commission on the Temporary Crisis and Transition Framework for State Aid measures to support the economy following the aggression against Ukraine by Russia (OJ C 101, 17.3.2023, p. 3), as amended by Commission Communication C(2023)8045 (OJ C 1188, 21.11.2023, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/C/2023/1188/oj).
